source.title: Mind the (Data) Gap: Evaluating Vision Systems in Small Data Applications
source.authors: Samuel Stevens; S. M. Rayeed; J. Kline

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates image-task accuracy across labeled-data amounts and vision-model inference FLOPs. It does not test held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit or predict power laws, or examine compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. It cites the original scaling-law papers as context.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about vision and multimodal task accuracy as training examples and inference FLOPs vary. Those results do not measure the loss, power-law fit, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation specified by V1–V7. Related task-accuracy scaling results are recorded as findings fitting no version. References to language-model scaling are background rather than new results.
record.test_reason: The study measures accuracy on ecological image tasks against labeled-example count and vision-encoder inference FLOPs. It reports no pretraining loss, no power-law fit or extrapolation, and no compute-optimal allocation. Its Section 4.2 contrast with language-model scaling is a discussion point, not a test of any version. Model scale also varies only across eight SigLIP checkpoints that mix model size and image resolution (45–700+ GFLOPs). That does not test V6 downstream predictability with pretraining scale or loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find vision encoders with SVMs improve steadily with labeled data while MLLMs plateau after ~10–30 examples. Scaling SigLIP compute gives modest gains relative to adding labeled data. They advocate explicit small-data evaluation. They also report that vision-only pretraining (DINOv2) beats language-supervised pretraining on Species/Age, and the reverse on Gestalt/Context/Behavior.
record.recipe_differences: This is an ecological computer-vision evaluation of task accuracy using few-shot MLLM prompts and SVMs over frozen vision embeddings. It does not use the original language-model loss-scaling method or fit scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with labeled-example count, model family, vision-model size/image size and pretraining supervision; performance also differs across task clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: MLLMs (Gemini Flash 2.0/1.5 8B, Qwen2-VL 7B, Qwen2.5-VL 72B) show no sustained gain from more in-context examples. Accuracy often stays near chance (~0.5) or declines by n=30–100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Few-shot in-context learning in MLLMs on fine-grained ecological binary tasks does not improve with example count beyond ~10.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen vision encoders with SVMs improve near-logarithmically with labeled examples from 3 to 100. For SigLIP, a 10× increase in labeled samples beats a 10× increase in inference FLOPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the small-data regime, linear-probe accuracy scales more with labeled data than with encoder size or inference compute.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Workshop: The 3rd Workshop on Imageomics: Discovering Biological Knowledge from Images Using AI
record.problems: The study evaluates accuracy on ecological classification tasks, not held-out language-model cross-entropy or fitted power laws. The compute comparison is for vision-model inference FLOPs, and plotted values are not numerically tabulated in the provided text. The task setting and benchmark do not test the original loss-scaling claims.
record.rows_left_out: The appendices report extensive per-model, per-task-cluster accuracy tables for multiple example counts (Tables 1–18), plus pretraining-supervision comparisons (Figures 3–4). These are not separately extracted because they report ecological task accuracy rather than a measure named by V1–V7; the relevant aggregate scaling patterns are represented by r1–r5.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss or power-law fits.
All: no extrapolation from small runs.
All: no shape-at-fixed-parameter comparison of loss.
All: no loss power laws in vision, fine-tuning or transfer; only task accuracy versus labeled-sample count.
Downstream predictability from pretraining scale or loss. Only a coarse inference-FLOPs comparison across SigLIP checkpoints is shown, with no fit.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from cites_only to discusses. Section 4.2 explicitly contrasts its findings with LM scaling laws (Kaplan, Hoffmann) and says they challenge 'bigger is better'. Still, no version is tested. Rows are correctly unlinked, but their values are available in Appendix Tables 1–18 rather than figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and the non-bottleneck conditions.
Prediction of large-run loss from power laws fitted on small runs.
Loss-minimizing parameter/token allocations at fixed compute and their scaling with compute.
Loss differences caused by depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds for held-out loss in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream performance predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, and bending of loss curves.

rows.subject: Gemini Flash 2.0
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean NeWT task accuracy while varying the number of labeled examples included in few-shot prompts.
rows.uncertainty: Bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals shown; numerical values not stated for this curve.
rows.note: The paper describes MLLMs as showing early gains and then plateaus after about 10–30 examples across most task clusters. This is task accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: Link to none is correct. Note that the appendix tables give numbers, e.g. Gemini Flash 2.0 Species 0.48 at n=100 versus 0.57 at n=3. So the curve is readable, not figure-only, and 'plateau' is often near chance (~0.5).
